newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate drops to 9.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate drops to 9.5 pct.

text.p: Abundant supply of kuna funds lowered Croatia's average money market rate to 9.5 percent from 10.8 percent on Thursday, dealers said.
The total daily trade was halved to 20.6 million kuna, of which 16.1 million were fresh borrowings. The end of trading left a surplus of 49.4 million kuna on the supply side.
Most of the trading were call money borrowings, whose rate also edged down to 9 percent from 9.44 percent.
Smaller short-term loans were made at rates of 11 percent and 14 percent.
There was no overnight trade on Wednesday as all banks were liquid.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Friday eased to 5.4565 against the dollar and 3.5624 against the mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
